business_problem: Merck wanted to reduce false rejects in pharmaceutical manufacturing so it could get life-saving drugs to customers faster while maintaining product safety.
solution_summary: Merck built a manufacturing analytics and AI pipeline on AWS to reduce false rejects in pharmaceutical production. Real-time data from manufacturing processes and inspection machines is ingested with Amazon Kinesis, transformed and contextualized with AWS Glue, and loaded into Amazon Redshift for analytics and dashboards in Amazon QuickSight. The company's AI/ML platform on Amazon SageMaker combines harmonized process data with defect images transferred through AWS DataSync so teams can analyze quality signals across sites, investigate anomalies quickly, and support root-cause analysis. This architecture gives Merck a shared data foundation for near-real-time decision-making while improving yield, product availability, and response times for investigations and corrective actions.

solution_components.name: AWS Glue
solution_components.role: Transforms and prepares data used by the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon Kinesis
solution_components.role: Streams near-real-time events into the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon Redshift
solution_components.role: Serves as the analytics warehouse for the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon QuickSight
solution_components.role: Presents dashboards and analytics for the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon SageMaker
solution_components.role: Builds, trains, or deploys the machine learning models behind the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

solution_components.name: AWS DataSync
solution_components.role: Transfers source files and images into the monitoring and anomaly-detection workflows.

data_flow: Merck ingests real-time manufacturing and inspection-machine data with Amazon Kinesis and AWS Glue, loads harmonized data into Amazon Redshift for dashboards in Amazon QuickSight, and uses Amazon SageMaker with defect images brought in through AWS DataSync to power quality analytics and AI/ML workflows.
business_outcome: By using AWS services, Merck improved product availability and yield while enabling faster investigations, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions across its manufacturing operations.
